purpose: Machine-readable inventory of every language, framework, library, model, and service NOBS uses. Read by humans learning the stack and by coding agents that need to know what this project already standardises on before proposing new code.
how_to_use: Agents: load this file before proposing a dependency or a pattern. Prefer an entry that already exists over introducing a new one. If a task genuinely needs something absent here, check 'alternatives' on the closest entry first, and respect 'constraints'.
constraints: Cross-platform is a hard requirement: shared backend code must run on Linux, macOS, and Windows/WSL2. A platform-only dependency belongs behind an adapter.
Local-first and privacy-first: prefer a local or on-device option over a hosted service. Do not add a dependency that phones home by default.
No dependency for something an Apple framework or the Python standard library already solves cleanly.
Every new integration must declare its data source, permissions, network destinations, retention, failure behavior, and revocation.

entries.name: Python
entries.role: Language for the Tank backend, CI tooling, and deploy scripts.
entries.why_here: 3.11 is the supported floor because the code uses StrEnum and modern typing syntax. CI exercises 3.11 and 3.12.
entries.learn: Start with the standard library's pathlib, dataclasses, enum, and asyncio - all four are used throughout app/.

entries.name: FastAPI
entries.role: HTTP API framework for the Tank: routing, validation, dependency injection, OpenAPI schema.
entries.why_here: Validates external input with typed models and generates the OpenAPI contract that the iPhone app and dashboard code against.

alternatives.name: Litestar
alternatives.when: Wanting built-in DI layers and stricter typing; similar performance profile.

alternatives.name: Flask + pydantic
alternatives.when: A much smaller surface with no async requirement.

alternatives.name: Django REST Framework
alternatives.when: You want an ORM, admin, and auth batteries included - heavier than this project needs.

entries.learn: The dependency-injection system is the part worth understanding: app/dependencies.py shows typed Annotated dependencies, which is the modern idiom.

entries.name: Uvicorn
entries.role: ASGI server that actually runs the FastAPI app.
entries.why_here: Standard ASGI server; the [standard] extra brings uvloop and httptools for speed on Linux.

alternatives.name: Hypercorn
alternatives.when: You need HTTP/2 or HTTP/3.

alternatives.name: Granian
alternatives.when: Rust-based server, worth benchmarking if throughput ever matters.

entries.learn: Understand the ASGI interface - it is the contract between Uvicorn and FastAPI.

entries.name: Pydantic
entries.role: Typed models for every request and response body.
entries.why_here: The wire contract in app/schemas.py is Pydantic models; validation at the boundary is a project rule.

alternatives.name: attrs + cattrs
alternatives.when: You want structuring without the validation layer.

alternatives.name: msgspec
alternatives.when: Serialization speed dominates; noticeably faster but a smaller ecosystem.

entries.learn: v2 is a near-rewrite of v1 in Rust - when reading Stack Overflow answers, check which version they target.

entries.name: pydantic-settings
entries.role: Loads all NOBS_* environment variables into the typed Settings object.
entries.why_here: Configuration is centralised in app/config.py by project rule; this makes env vars typed and documented in one place.

alternatives.name: python-decouple
alternatives.when: A much simpler project with no typing needs.

alternatives.name: dynaconf
alternatives.when: You need layered config files per environment.

entries.learn: Settings resolves paths relative to the working directory - which is exactly why tests/conftest.py chdir's into a temp dir.

entries.name: HTTPX
entries.role: Async and sync HTTP client for Ollama, Home Assistant, weather, and page fetching.
entries.why_here: Async support and a pluggable transport, which is what lets tests inject MockTransport instead of hitting the network.

alternatives.name: aiohttp
alternatives.when: Async-only and you want a websocket client in the same library.

alternatives.name: requests
alternatives.when: Sync-only scripts; no async support at all.

entries.learn: MockTransport is the single most useful testing feature here - see how tests/test_chat.py uses it.

entries.name: SQLite (stdlib sqlite3)
entries.role: Local store for approvals, proposals, audit events, briefings, schedules, and dream-team state.
entries.why_here: Local-first: a single file on the Tank, no server to run, no data leaving the house. 14 tables defined in app/agent_schema.py.

alternatives.name: DuckDB
alternatives.when: Analytical queries over the research library rather than transactional writes.

alternatives.name: Postgres
alternatives.when: Multiple writers across machines - would break the local-first single-appliance model.

entries.learn: WAL mode (set in the schema) is why reads do not block writes. Note SQLite cannot add a NOT NULL column without a default - that shapes the migration list.

entries.name: python-zeroconf
entries.role: Advertises the Tank over mDNS/Bonjour so devices can find it without a hardcoded IP.
entries.why_here: Discovery on the local network with no cloud round-trip.

alternatives.name: avahi via D-Bus
alternatives.when: Linux-only deployment; not cross-platform.

entries.learn: Registration is synchronous and runs on its own loop - main.py deliberately pushes it to a thread so mDNS cannot block startup.

entries.name: psutil
entries.role: CPU, memory, and disk readings for Tank health and optimizer idle detection.
entries.why_here: Cross-platform system metrics; the optimizer only runs heavy jobs when CPU is genuinely idle.

alternatives.name: Reading /proc directly
alternatives.when: Linux-only and you want zero dependencies.

entries.learn: cpu_percent() needs an interval or a prior call to mean anything - a common source of wrong readings.

entries.name: ddgs (DuckDuckGo Search)
entries.role: Web search backing the agent's web_search tool.
entries.why_here: No API key and no account, which keeps the free local core genuinely free.

alternatives.name: SearXNG
alternatives.when: You want to self-host search on the Tank - strong local-first fit, worth evaluating.

alternatives.name: Brave Search API
alternatives.when: You need reliability guarantees and can accept an API key.

alternatives.name: Tavily
alternatives.when: LLM-oriented search results; hosted and paid.

entries.learn: Unofficial scraping clients break when the upstream HTML changes - this is the most fragile runtime dependency in the project.

entries.name: trafilatura
entries.role: Extracts readable article text from a fetched HTML page.
entries.why_here: Turns a page into something a small local model can actually read.

alternatives.name: readability-lxml
alternatives.when: Lighter dependency, somewhat lower extraction quality.

alternatives.name: Playwright + custom extraction
alternatives.when: The page needs JavaScript to render.

entries.learn: NOBS fetches with httpx first and disables redirects, so an allowed public URL cannot 302 into the LAN - trafilatura's own fetch_url would follow it.

entries.name: feedparser
entries.role: Parses RSS and Atom feeds for the news tool.
entries.why_here: Handles the many malformed feeds in the wild without special cases.

alternatives.name: atoma
alternatives.when: You want stricter parsing and typed output.

entries.learn: It never raises on a bad feed - it sets a bozo flag. Silence is not success.

entries.name: Wikipedia-API
entries.role: Fetches Wikipedia article summaries for the lookup_wikipedia tool.
entries.why_here: A cited, stable reference source for the research library.

alternatives.name: MediaWiki API directly
alternatives.when: You need search, categories, or revisions rather than summaries.

entries.learn: Always send a descriptive user agent - Wikimedia blocks generic ones.

entries.name: pytest
entries.role: The backend test suite - 249 tests covering routes, auth, tools, and failure paths.
entries.why_here: Fixtures make the hermetic-environment pattern in conftest.py possible, which is what keeps tests from touching real Tank data.

alternatives.name: unittest
alternatives.when: Standard library only; far more boilerplate.

entries.learn: Read tests/conftest.py first - the autouse fixture explains why every test runs in a temp directory with NOBS_* env vars stripped.

entries.name: Ruff
entries.role: Linter and formatter for all Python, enforced in CI.
entries.why_here: Replaces flake8, isort, pyupgrade, and black with one fast Rust tool.

alternatives.name: black + flake8 + isort
alternatives.when: The older split toolchain; slower and three configs.

entries.learn: The rule set is pinned explicitly in pyproject.toml. Without an explicit select, a Ruff upgrade silently changes what CI enforces - that happened here and produced 61 surprise failures.

entries.name: uv
entries.role: Fast resolver; uv.lock pins the full backend dependency graph.
entries.why_here: Reproducible installs across Linux, macOS, and Windows.

alternatives.name: pip + requirements.txt
alternatives.when: What scripts/dev.py uses today for the venv install.

alternatives.name: Poetry
alternatives.when: You want dependency groups and publishing in one tool.

entries.learn: From the same team as Ruff. Note dev.py currently installs with pip, so uv.lock is a pin record rather than the install path.

entries.name: Hatchling
entries.role: PEP 517 build backend that packages the app/ directory.
entries.why_here: Minimal configuration for a simple package.

alternatives.name: setuptools
alternatives.when: Maximum compatibility with old tooling.

entries.learn: The build backend only matters at install time - it is not a runtime dependency.

entries.name: Swift 6
entries.role: Language for the iPhone app, widgets, and the macOS Tank supervisor.
entries.why_here: Native Apple development; strict concurrency checking catches data races at compile time.

alternatives.name: React Native / Flutter
alternatives.when: Cross-platform mobile - rejected here because the app is deliberately Apple-native.

entries.learn: Swift 6 strict concurrency is the big learning curve: @MainActor, Sendable, and actor isolation. See the axiom-concurrency skill.

entries.name: SwiftUI
entries.role: The entire iPhone and macOS interface.
entries.why_here: Declarative UI with Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, and reduced-motion support built in - accessibility is a product requirement, not an add-on.

alternatives.name: UIKit
alternatives.when: Fine-grained control or older OS targets; can be bridged where needed.

entries.learn: Keep views small and move state into observable models - the project rule exists because large views become untestable.

entries.name: FoundationModels
entries.role: Apple's on-device language model, used for local processing when Tank is unavailable.
entries.why_here: Keeps the 'Local' processing route genuinely local.

alternatives.name: Core ML with a bundled model
alternatives.when: You need a specific model rather than the system one.

entries.learn: Guard the import - it is not available on every OS version the project builds for.

entries.name: App Intents
entries.role: Exposes NOBS actions to Siri, Shortcuts, and Spotlight.
entries.why_here: The 'same assistant everywhere' promise starts with Siri on Apple devices.

alternatives.name: SiriKit Intents
alternatives.when: The older API; App Intents supersedes it.

entries.learn: App Intents replaced SiriKit for most cases - check the date on any tutorial you read.

entries.name: WidgetKit + ActivityKit
entries.role: Home/Lock Screen widgets and Live Activities for approvals and briefings.
entries.why_here: Passive daily context and live tracking of unfolding workflows.
entries.learn: Widgets run in a separate process with a tight memory budget - they read a snapshot file rather than calling the API.

entries.name: StoreKit 2
entries.role: In-app tips and the NOBScloud subscription.
entries.why_here: Required by App Store rules for digital purchases.

alternatives.name: Square / Stripe
alternatives.when: Payments outside the app - already used for web tips.

entries.learn: StoreKit 2 is async/await and much simpler than the original API. Test with the local .storekit configuration file before touching App Store Connect.

entries.name: EventKit
entries.role: Reads calendar events and reminders for the daily briefing.
entries.why_here: The briefing is the product anchor and needs the real schedule.
entries.learn: Permissions are progressive by product rule - request access at the moment its value is clear, not at launch.

entries.name: Xcode 27
entries.role: Builds and tests all Apple targets.
entries.why_here: The only supported toolchain for iOS and macOS.
entries.learn: Apple builds cannot run on Linux, which is why the iOS CI job uses a self-hosted Mac runner.

entries.name: React 19
entries.role: The public website at nobsdash.com.
entries.why_here: Component model for the marketing and portfolio site.

alternatives.name: Astro
alternatives.when: A content site that ships almost no JavaScript - arguably a better fit for a marketing page.

alternatives.name: Svelte
alternatives.when: Smaller bundles and less ceremony.

entries.learn: React 19 adds Actions and the use() hook; older tutorials will not mention them.

entries.name: Vite 6
entries.role: Dev server and production bundler for the website.
entries.why_here: Fast dev server and a simple production build.

alternatives.name: Next.js
alternatives.when: You need SSR, routing, and an image pipeline.

entries.learn: Dev uses native ES modules while the production build uses Rollup - behavior can differ between them.

entries.name: pnpm
entries.role: Installs website dependencies.
entries.why_here: Content-addressed store, so disk use stays low and installs are fast.

alternatives.name: npm
alternatives.when: Preinstalled with Node; slower and larger on disk.

entries.learn: pnpm's strict node_modules layout catches dependencies you use but never declared.

entries.name: @phosphor-icons/react
entries.role: Icon set for the website.
entries.why_here: A consistent icon family, so no hand-drawn SVGs or emoji in the UI.

alternatives.name: Lucide
alternatives.when: You prefer a Feather-derived look.

entries.learn: Import icons individually so the bundler can tree-shake the rest of the set.

entries.name: Ollama
entries.role: Runs local language models on the Tank; every model call goes through its HTTP API.
entries.why_here: The entire local-first promise depends on inference that never leaves the house.

alternatives.name: llama.cpp server
alternatives.when: You want maximum control over quantization and sampling.

alternatives.name: vLLM
alternatives.when: Serving many concurrent users on a GPU - overkill for one household.

alternatives.name: LM Studio
alternatives.when: A GUI for experimenting rather than a service.

entries.learn: Ollama supports JSON-schema-constrained decoding, which this project uses instead of free-form JSON mode - it is the difference between hoping for valid JSON and requiring it.

entries.name: qwen3:8b
entries.role: Default general chat and agent model.
entries.why_here: Fits comfortably in Tank memory while still following tool-call instructions.

alternatives.name: llama3.1:8b
alternatives.when: A general-purpose alternative at the same size.

alternatives.name: mistral-small
alternatives.when: Worth benchmarking for instruction following.

entries.learn: Model choice is configuration, not code - NOBS_OLLAMA_MODEL swaps it without touching app/.

entries.name: qwen2.5-coder:14b
entries.role: Code-oriented model for log analysis and the dream-team sandbox.
entries.why_here: Better at structured and code output than the general 8b model.

alternatives.name: deepseek-coder-v2
alternatives.when: Worth comparing on code generation quality.

entries.learn: A 14b model needs roughly twice the memory of an 8b at the same quantization - the constraint is RAM, not disk.

entries.name: nomic-embed-text
entries.role: Embedding model for the research library index.
entries.why_here: Local embeddings mean research can be searched without uploading it anywhere.

alternatives.name: bge-m3
alternatives.when: You need multilingual embeddings.

entries.learn: Embeddings are how semantic search works: text becomes a vector, and similarity is distance between vectors.

entries.name: Home Assistant
entries.role: Bridge to smart-home devices; NOBS calls its REST API rather than talking to vendors directly.
entries.why_here: One local integration instead of one cloud account per device brand.

alternatives.name: Matter/Thread directly
alternatives.when: Long-term direction; avoids the Home Assistant dependency entirely.

alternatives.name: HomeKit via HAP
alternatives.when: Apple-only households.

entries.learn: Home tools are risk-classified: lights and media are one class, locks and cameras another that always needs approval.

entries.name: GitHub Actions
entries.role: Runs the gating test/lint check on the self-hosted Mac, an advisory Linux/macOS/Windows matrix on hosted runners, and iOS tests on the Mac.
entries.why_here: Free on public repositories, and the cross-platform matrix is how the hard cross-platform requirement is actually enforced when hosted runners are available.

alternatives.name: GitLab CI / Woodpecker
alternatives.when: Self-hosting the whole pipeline.

entries.learn: Actions is free and unlimited on standard hosted runners for public repos - a hosted job that dies in seconds with runner_id 0 and no logs is an account-level hold, not a charge for this repo. The gating check runs on a self-hosted runner so that condition can never block a pull request. See docs/research/COSTS.md.

entries.name: systemd
entries.role: Keeps the Tank API, dashboard, and tunnel running and restarts them on failure.
entries.why_here: The Tank is an always-on appliance; services must survive reboots.

alternatives.name: launchd
alternatives.when: macOS - already used by scripts/install-tank-launchagent.sh.

entries.learn: journalctl -u nobs-api is the first command to run when the Tank misbehaves.

entries.name: cloudflared
entries.role: Tunnels the public marketing site out from the Tank.
entries.why_here: Publishes a website with no inbound ports opened on the home network.

alternatives.name: Tailscale Funnel
alternatives.when: You are already on Tailscale.

alternatives.name: WireGuard
alternatives.when: Private remote access rather than public publishing.

entries.learn: Only the marketing site is tunnelled. The API port is deliberately not proxied - a proxy in front of it would make every remote request look local and break the pairing gate.

entries.name: qrcode
entries.role: Renders the pairing QR code so a phone can claim the Tank without typing a token.
entries.why_here: The device token is long by design; a QR code keeps first-run pairing bearable without weakening it.

alternatives.name: segno
alternatives.when: Pure Python with no Pillow dependency for image output.

entries.learn: It is a dev/setup dependency, not a runtime one - the API never generates QR codes itself.
